claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children under the age of 16, or children aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - Alex, who's 8 years old. I'm interested in finding out if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to know that Alex is 8 years old.

Now, to assess your eligibility, I need to understand your living situation:

**Do you currently live with Alex in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me at the moment. I do help out financially when I can though - I contribute towards things for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to understand your financial contributions better, as this is important for eligibility.

**Roughly how much do you contribute each month towards Alex's upkeep (such as food, clothes, pocket money, or other essentials), and how does this compare to the current Child Benefit rate?**

(Just to give you context, the current Child Benefit rate is £23.80 per week for the first child, which works out to approximately £103 per month.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute about £10 a week towards Alex - so around £40 a month. I help with things like clothes and a few essentials when I can, but it's not as much as the Child Benefit rate you mentioned.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I now have a clearer picture of your situation.

Before I make my final assessment, I need to ask one more important question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or are you the only person who might be claiming for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm the only one - no one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility.

Let me explain the outcome:

Based on the rules for Child Benefit when a child lives with someone else, you would normally qualify for Child Benefit for 8 weeks after your child goes to live with someone else, if nobody else claims. However, to continue receiving Child Benefit beyond those initial 8 weeks, you would need to contribute towards Alex's upkeep by **at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment itself** (approximately £23.80 per week or £103 per month).

Since you're currently contributing around £10 per week (£40 per month), which is less than the Child Benefit rate, you would not meet the threshold needed to continue claiming beyond the initial 8-week period.

Additionally, the rules state that you're usually responsible for a child if you live with them OR if you're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards their care. Since your contributions fall short of this threshold, you wouldn't qualify for ongoing Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

The key issue is that your financial contributions don't meet the required threshold. To be responsible for a child who doesn't live with you, you need to be contributing at least as much as the Child Benefit payment itself. Your contributions of £10 per week fall short of the £23.80 per week needed.

However, if your circumstances change and you're able to increase your contributions to at least £23.80 per week (or if Alex were to come and live with you), you could then become eligible. In that case, I'd recommend contacting the Child Benefit Office to update them on your changed circumstances.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
